title: Uniform amplitude of proper direct image on classical finite-coefficient complexes
statement:
Let $A$ be a finite commutative ring with the discrete topology and $f:X\to Y$ a proper morphism of schemes. Suppose $e\in\mathbf N$ bounds the Krull dimension of every fibre after every base change [def-weil-proper-morphism] [def-pc-base-change] [def-kun-topological-krull-dimension]. For $T=X,Y$ let $\mathcal A_T=\operatorname{Mod}(T_{\mathrm{pro\acute et}},A_T)$ and $D_T=D(\mathcal A_T)$ be the ordinary constant-$A$ module-sheaf categories and their unbounded derived categories, in a common universe in which the sites and all indexing families under consideration are small [def-weil-pbc-proetale-modules] [sk-def-sfb-derived-categories]. Write $G=Rf_{\mathrm{pro\acute et},*}$ for total K-injective direct image and use the classical-cohomology predicate of [sk-def-pe-classical-definition].
Then $G$ is triangulated, commutes with integer shifts, and preserves countable products with their canonical projections. For every integer $a$ and every $L\in D_X$, $L\in D_X^{\ge a}$ implies $G L\in D_Y^{\ge a}$. For every integer $b$ and every classical-cohomology $L\in D_X$, $L\in D_X^{\le b}$ implies $G L\in D_Y^{\le b+2e}$, even when $L$ is unbounded below. On the small étale sites with constant $A$ coefficients, $R^qf_{\mathrm{\acute et},*}F=0$ for every $A$-module sheaf $F$ and $q>2e$, with higher direct images as in [def-weil-pbc-direct-image]. The degree inequalities refer to the standard t-structures [def-sbc-standard-tstructure-derived-category]. No quasi-compactness of $Y$ or bound on the cohomological dimension of a ground field is required. Moreover, the total étale direct image $E=Rf_{\mathrm{\acute et},*}:D(X_{\mathrm{\acute et}},A)\to D(Y_{\mathrm{\acute et}},A)$ preserves every small ambient coproduct, with the canonical comparison whose components are $E$ of the coprojections [def-weil-pbc-derived-categories].

proof.text: Apply the ringed-site Grothendieck and K-injective existence theorem to the actual constant ring sheaves. The canonical constant-ring pullback/direct-image adjunction agrees with the sectionwise coefficient direct image: this follows from the hom-equivalence inverse equations and the defining coefficient map. Derive that adjunction. Its right adjoint preserves all existing products. Generic K-injective derived products supply countable products in both derived categories, and the additive total derived functor is triangulated and commutes with integer shifts.

source.place: Setup and Transfer: total derived module direct image and its canonical products

proof.text: For a complex L bounded below by a, regard L as an object of the bounded-below derived category. Negative vanishing for the additive direct image kills homology below a. Transport this vanishing along the canonical total/bounded-below derived-functor compatibility. Thus the total direct image has the same lower bound.

The underlying additive group of a finite coefficient ring is torsion, and every module over it is torsion. Apply this sectionwise to any etale coefficient module sheaf. The identity base change identifies the original fibres with those in the assumed base-change bound, by the canonical fibre isomorphism. Proper torsion vanishing therefore applies. The higher-direct-image forgetful comparison identifies the forgotten module higher image with the vanishing abelian higher image. Faithful additive forgetting reflects the zero object by reflecting the equality identity = zero. This gives etale vanishing for every integer q > 2e.

source.place: Etale statements: uniform 2e vanishing; Stacks Tags 095U and 0D6J

proof.text: Use the proved exact restriction equivalence along constant scalar sections and its derived direct-image comparison, supplied by the private helpers of the classical-direct-image-preservation module. A classical intrinsic module sheaf H restricts to a classical fixed-ring module sheaf. The essential-image characterization writes it as comparison pullback of an etale sheaf E. Properness supplies qcqs, so the bounded-below direct-image comparison applies to E[0]. Compose it with exact restriction/single-functor compatibility and total/bounded-below compatibility. Exact comparison pullback preserves the upper bound 2e proved in the previous step. Faithful exact restriction reflects vanishing of each homology object. Hence the intrinsic total image of H[0] is bounded above by 2e.

source.place: Transfer: classical heart objects and bounded-below comparison

proof.text: Products of pro-etale modules are exact. Thus the ordinary derived category is left complete: every complex is the homotopy limit of its truncations in degrees at least -n. Use the existing homotopy-limit lemma with the chosen product fan, and identify its lift and tower shift with the canonical Pi.lift and towerTransitionEndomorphism by their projection equations. Apply the left-complete heart upper-bound theorem to the class of classical module sheaves, the heart bound 2e above, and product preservation. It combines finite Postnikov induction with eventual invertibility of homology transitions, giving the sharp bound b + 2e for every classical-cohomology complex bounded above by b, without a lower bound.

source.place: Transfer and truncation argument; Stacks Tags 07KC, 08TB, 08TC and 0H72

proof.text: Apply the finite-relative-cohomological-dimension etale coproduct criterion with c = 2e. Properness supplies qcqs. Convert the integer vanishing on the degree-zero single functor to the natural-degree right-derived-functor formulation by the standard homology/right-derived isomorphism. The criterion gives preservation of every small coproduct, through its canonical comparison, including empty families.
